answer: Because the walnut ledger attributes every share, the vine audit exposes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 60% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, which means it pays the anchor fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 4 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
